policy_title: Universities Duty of Care for Students and Mental Health Charter
stated: Safeguard the future of our world-leading universities and the wellbeing of every student by: Giving higher education institutions a statutory duty of care for their students. Introducing a statutory Student Mental Health Charter and requiring universities to make mental health services accessible to their students.

source.quote: Safeguard the future of our world-leading universities and the wellbeing of every student by: Supporting science, research and innovation in universities, including continuing to participate in Horizon Europe and joining the European Innovation Council, as set out in chapter 4. Giving higher education institutions a statutory duty of care for their students. Introducing a statutory Student Mental Health Charter and requiring universities to make mental health services accessible to their students.

bearing_set.reason: Requires universities to make mental health services accessible and introduces a statutory mental health charter — a direct intervention in healthcare access for a large population of students.

Student mental health is a material driver of dropout, attainment, and the opportunity gap; a statutory duty of care with enforceable mental health provision plausibly earns a real verdict on educational outcomes and opportunity.

membership_note: O3 is the primary bearing (mental health service access is healthcare). O7 is a genuine secondary bearing via the completion/attainment mechanism. No direct tax, spending, or liberty mechanism is specified, so O11, O12, and O10 do not reach the non-negligible bar.
